bib.title: PandaLM: An Automatic Evaluation Benchmark for LLM Instruction Tuning Optimization

question: Can an open, locally run judge LLM replace human or API judges to pick better hyperparameters for instruction tuning?
hypothesis: A judge LLM trained on filtered GPT-3.5 pairwise labels with reasons can match GPT-3.5/GPT-4 agreement with humans and yield better-tuned models than Alpaca defaults.
contributions: PandaLM, a privacy-protected judge LM for evaluating and optimizing LLM hyperparameters
A human-annotated test set for validating PandaLM
Use of PandaLM to tune hyperparameters of open LLMs, beating Alpaca's defaults

method.summary: A LLaMA-based judge is fine-tuned on 300K GPT-3.5-distilled pairwise comparisons (verdict, reason, reference answer) after dropping order-inconsistent labels. It is validated against a 1K human-labelled test set and then used to pick among 80 hyperparameter configs for five 7B-class base models.
method.task: pairwise response evaluation (win/lose/tie) and hyperparameter selection for instruction tuning

datasets.name: PandaLM training data
datasets.source: instructions and inputs from Alpaca 52K; response pairs from five Alpaca-tuned models; labels from gpt-3.5-turbo
datasets.preprocessing: hand-crafted rules remove invalid outputs; samples dropped when verdict conflicts after swapping response order

datasets.name: Human-labelled test set
datasets.size: 1K samples (2.5K before filtering); 105 ties, 422 response-1 wins, 472 response-2 wins
datasets.source: self-instruct human-evaluation inputs; three annotators from an annotation company
datasets.preprocessing: samples with annotator divergence removed so IAA >0.85

datasets.name: LSAT / PubMedQA / BioASQ
datasets.source: public datasets; responses from Vicuna and Alpaca; GPT-4 as gold judge

models.name: PandaLM-7B
models.architecture: LLaMA backbone, seq2seq with next-token loss

models.name: LLaMA-7B, Bloom-7B, Cerebras-GPT-6.7B, OPT-7B, Pythia-6.9B
models.architecture: decoder-only, each tuned on Alpaca data with Alpaca hyperparameters, then tuned over 80 configs

training.objective: standard cross-entropy next-token prediction, seq2seq, no classification head
training.batch_size: 2 per GPU, gradient accumulation 8 steps (inferred: 128 effective on 8 GPUs)

other.alpaca_baseline: 3 epochs, final checkpoint, AdamW, lr 2e-5, cosine
other.search_space: checkpoints epoch 1-5; lr 2e-6, 1e-5, 2e-5, 2e-4; SGD or AdamW; cosine or linear = 80 configs

inference.samples: each pair judged twice with order swapped; conflicts set to Tie; 800 comparisons for the search
inference.prompting: Alpaca-style instruction/input/response1/response2 template, outputs verdict then reason then reference

other.search_procedure: 80 configs split into 4 blocks of 20; sequential comparison within block, then winners compared

metrics.name: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 vs human
metrics.definition: three-class win/lose/tie agreement with human labels; averaging scheme for P/R/F1 not stated

metrics.name: win/lose/tie counts
metrics.definition: pairwise counts between tuned models on 170 instructions

baselines: untuned LLaMA and Vicuna log-likelihood judging
eval.protocol: Judges vs human labels on 1K human-labelled test set; downstream tuned models judged by GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and human experts. Single run, no seeds or significance tests stated.

limits: Hyperparameter ranges follow common practice and may miss the optimum (Sec 6).
Training labels come from GPT-3.5 and may not match human preference (Sec 6).
Only outcome-based evaluation, which is resource-intensive; supervised training only.
PandaLM-7B accuracy (0.5926) is below GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 despite the 'comparable' wording.
Domain tests use GPT-4 as gold, not humans (30-sample human check on BioASQ only).
Hyperparameter search uses PandaLM-7B, not 70B, for compute reasons.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; no code/weights/data link in the text.
